 By Andrew Chesterton Updated October 26 2026 - 4:02pm , first published 11:00am By Andrew Chesterton Updated October 26 2026 - 4:02pm , first published 11:00am Save Share The long history of the Pajero's new engine Mitsubishi has worked wonders with one of its oldest engine families in the all-new Pajero, with the brand's "newly developed" diesel donk tracing its history back to 2015 and the Triton ute, which launched as the 4N15 engine.

 And now, in Pajero guise, the brand has returned to single turbocharging, though still managing to increase maximum torque to 480Nm. It's a decade-plus run for one of the brand's most well-known engine families, and it seems history will soon repeat with the Triton almost certain to adopt Pajero power from its next update.

 "It's a new generation of the 4N16, and the main thing is to be able to comply with Euro 6D regulations. And then also, the other reason that happened is to be able to pair that engine with the 8-speed transmission," says Rob Pinedo, Pajero Product Manager, who also confirms the same core engine has now powered two generations of Triton and one of Pajero.
 Asked whether the facelifted Triton would feature the same engine, Mr Pinedo replied: "That may happen".
 + 2 "There's going to be a point in time where every car you sell, every new car you sell, then has to comply with Euro 6D," he says.
 This engine breaths new life into the Pajero
 If that engine sounds like the one old-fashioned part of the Pajero story, it shouldn't. After a brief off-road drive we felt the combination of a smooth eight-speed transmission, what must be a ton of insulation and sound-deadening, and the light bump in torque makes the Pajero's engine feel far fresher and more smooth than even the dual-stage turbo equivalent in the Triton.
 It's a big moment for Mitsubishi in Australia. The brand hasn't had much to crow about in the past few years, but the return of the Pajero nameplate is a significant moment.
 "I've been working for Mitsubishi for 35 years, and I'm very much a Mitsubishi person," says Shunichi Kihara, Mitsubishi Australia CEO. 
 "Therefore, to see the return of this iconic name in our lineup is super, super exciting. And the product itself is also very encouraging. We believe that Pajero has a lot of strengths and features and character, so having this iconic name with that level of product competitiveness is a very, very exciting moment."
